text: Copyright is the exclusive legal right to reproduce, distribute, perform, display, and create derivative works from original creative expressions. Under the Copyright Act 1957, copyright protects: literary works (books, manuals, software code), artistic works (paintings, drawings, photographs, logos), musical works (compositions), dramatic works (plays, scripts), cinematograph films, and sound recordings. For AYUSH sector, copyright protects: research papers and publications, product manuals and inserts, marketing brochures and catalogs, training videos, photographs of products and processes, software for formulation management, original artwork on packaging. Copyright does NOT protect ideas, facts, procedures, or methods — only the expression.

Copyright registration in India: 1) File application online at copyright.gov.in with Form XIV and prescribed fees. 2) Attach two copies of the work (physical or digital). 3) Mandatory 30-day waiting period for any objections. 4) Examination by Copyright Office — may raise queries. 5) If no objection, registration certificate issued. Timeline: 2-4 months typically. Registration is NOT mandatory for copyright protection (copyright exists automatically upon creation), but registration provides prima facie evidence of ownership, useful in infringement lawsuits. For AYUSH companies: register important works like flagship publications, unique marketing content, and software.

Copyright duration in India: Literary, dramatic, musical, and artistic works: author's lifetime + 60 years (after death). Photographs: 60 years from publication. Cinematograph films: 60 years from publication. Sound recordings: 60 years from publication. Government works: 60 years from publication. Anonymous/pseudonymous works: 60 years from publication. After expiry, works enter public domain. For AYUSH: traditional Ayurvedic texts like Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita are in public domain (ancient). Modern commentaries, translations, and original compilations can have fresh copyright as derivative works.

Copyright registration fees (2024): Literary/dramatic/musical/artistic work: Rs 500 per work. Cinematograph film: Rs 5,000 per work. Sound recording: Rs 2,000 per work. Software: Rs 500 per work. Multiple works in same application: fees multiply. Waiting period objection response: included. Certified copy of registration: Rs 500. Recordal of changes (assignment, license): Rs 500. Much cheaper than patents or trademarks — register all important creative assets.

Copyright and patent protect different aspects: COPYRIGHT — expression of ideas (how something is written/drawn/filmed), automatic protection upon creation, long duration (60+ years), narrow scope (exact copying only), easy/cheap registration. PATENT — technical inventions (how something works), requires filing and examination, 20 years, broad scope (covers equivalents), expensive and slow. For AYUSH formulation research: Patent the novel formulation/process (if patentable). Copyright the research paper describing it. Copyright the software that calculates dosages. Both can coexist and complement each other.

Copyright infringement occurs when someone reproduces, distributes, performs, or creates derivative works without authorization. Types: Direct infringement (actual copying), Contributory infringement (facilitating others' copying), Vicarious infringement (profiting from others' copying). Remedies under Copyright Act 1957: Injunction (stop infringement), Damages (monetary compensation), Account of profits, Delivery up/destruction of infringing copies. Criminal penalties: imprisonment up to 3 years, fine up to Rs 2 lakh. For AYUSH sector: common infringement includes copying product manuals, unauthorized use of photographs, plagiarizing research content.

Section 52 of Copyright Act 1957 provides exceptions (similar to fair use): Private/personal use, Criticism/review with acknowledgment, Reporting current events, Reproduction for judicial proceedings, Reproduction by teachers for educational purposes, Reading/recitation in public with acknowledgment, Parody (limited), Research/private study. For AYUSH sector: quoting excerpts from Ayurvedic texts for educational purposes is generally permitted. Using competitor's copyrighted photos in your marketing is NOT fair use. When in doubt, seek permission or create original content.

Databases can be protected as compilations under copyright if the selection and arrangement is original. The individual data points may not be copyrightable, but the database structure/organization can be. Section 2(o) of Copyright Act includes 'computer databases' in the definition of literary works. For AYUSH: A database of traditional formulations with original classification system, cross-references, and annotations can be copyrighted. The underlying traditional knowledge itself is not protected. Sui generis database protection (like EU) does not exist in India — rely on copyright for the compilation.

Section 57 of Copyright Act 1957 grants moral rights (separate from economic rights): Right of paternity (attribution) — author's right to be credited as author. Right of integrity — right to prevent distortion, mutilation, or modification prejudicial to author's honor/reputation. Moral rights are perpetual (survive copyright expiry) and cannot be assigned (only economic rights can be). For AYUSH researchers: even if you assign copyright in your research paper to a publisher, you retain moral rights — publisher must credit you as author and cannot distort your findings.

Assignment (Section 18) — transfer of ownership of copyright, assignee becomes the new owner, must be in writing and signed. License (Section 30) — permission to use, licensor retains ownership, can be exclusive or non-exclusive. For AYUSH companies: typically license photographs from photographers (retain on your website with permission), assign copyright in work-for-hire content created by employees (check employment contracts), and get written assignments from freelance content creators. Always document IP assignments/licenses in writing to avoid disputes.
